scope: Focused GitHub search for customerless mining, useful-compute, resource-provider, and posted-reward mechanisms. Repository presence is not runtime permission or profitability evidence.

promoted.reason: Actively maintained open-source RandomX/KawPow/CryptoNight/GhostRider miner with built-in RandomX benchmarking. Suitable for exact-resource benchmarking on explicitly owned hardware.

Permissionless, trustless Monero pool with direct wallet payouts, 0% pool fee, 0 payout fee and documented small minimum payout. Strongest current first-dollar mining rail once exact owned-hardware economics are measured.

Active codebase whose README states Gridcoin rewards BOINC participation. Could monetize scientific compute instead of pure hashing. Exact newcomer/pool/bootstrap and withdrawability path must be verified before execution.

Provider nodes sell idle compute and receive GLM under pay-as-you-go/pay-per-task payment regimes. No customer acquisition is required, but revenue depends on marketplace demand, so it stays secondary to protocol-paid work.

Actively maintained CPU/GPU profit switcher that can incorporate electricity price and stop unprofitable mining. Useful architecture for Yield Harvester, but it automatically manages many third-party miner binaries and charges a developer fee; do not install wholesale without supply-chain review.
Use public market data to convert token rewards into realistic liquid-dollar estimates and identify apparent spreads. No order placement or credentials in the zero-capital lane.

research_only.reason: Repository documents regular BANANO payments for valid distributed proof-of-work solutions, but the repo has not been pushed since 2024. Treat as a potentially valuable customerless compute mechanism only after current service and payout verification.
Storage-node payouts exist, but earnings depend on customer storage/egress demand. Evaluate only against genuinely spare owned storage and marginal power/network cost.
Hostd tracks storage-provider revenue, but Sia hosting uses contract collateral and public network services. Zero-capital bootstrap and network-exposure constraints keep it behind Storj.
Runs a dVPN provider node and settles provider traffic, but it explicitly requires network exposure and terms acceptance. Residential-IP abuse/property risk keeps this out of automatic execution.

Bounties can pay 2-5 days after reward, but claiming requires public issue comments, a PR, and generally a demo video. Valuable posted-money lane, not passive/customerless enough for current priority.

rejected_or_parked.reason: Current repository contains only a minimal README and PostgreSQL mining-runtime persistence design notes. Its own scope says it does not add a production driver, scheduler, blockchain settlement, payment processing or account provisioning.

Source contains concealment/persistence features and an obfuscated remote native-payload loader that downloads encrypted PE bytes, manually maps them into memory and executes them. Do not install or execute.
Provider daemon requires a Kubernetes cluster, on-chain provider configuration, bid execution and transaction signing. Not a zero-capital first-dollar path.
Useful execution infrastructure for arbitrage/market making, but live strategies require funded positions, credentials and trading risk.
Core protocol client is useful infrastructure but consumer-GPU Bitcoin mining is not a realistic first-dollar lane.
Decentralized hosting/transport infrastructure without an inherent reward mechanism for serving content.
Historical implementation with no current reward, liquidity or maintained-network evidence established.

next_order: Verify current Gridcoin zero-capital newcomer/pool payout path.
Verify whether BoomPoW contributor payments are still live in 2026.
Benchmark XMRig RandomX on an explicitly owned CPU only; measure wall-power delta.
Use P2Pool payout mechanics for first-withdrawable-dollar modeling.
Add Golem provider economics as a secondary marketplace candidate.
Use CCXT public data to convert every crypto reward into liquid-dollar and withdrawal-threshold terms.
